chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Mithammi, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was sitting upon a chattel (carpet/furnishing), so I began to touch the chattel with my hand. He said: 'This which you are touching with your hand, is Armenian.' I said to him: 'And what have you to do with the Armenian?' He said: 'This is a chattel which the mother of Ali, a wife of his, brought with her.' So when it was another time, I entered upon him and began to touch what was beneath me. He said: 'It is as if you want to see what is beneath you.' I said: 'No, but the blind tend to tamper (or feel around).' He said to me: 'That chattel was for the mother of Ali, and she used to hold the opinion of the Khawarij, so I kept her for a night until morning, that she might retract from her opinion and accept the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), but she refrained from me. So when it was morning, I divorced her.'

key_terms.أَرْمَنِيٌّ: Armenian; referring to the origin of the carpet/furnishing.
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful; title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أُمُّ عَلِيٍّ: Mother of Ali; a title for one of the Imam's wives.
key_terms.رَأْيَ الْخَوَارِج: The opinion of the Khawarij; a theological/political sect.
key_terms.مَتَاع: Chattel, furniture, or carpet; personal property brought by a wife.

ai.seo_question: What is the story behind Imam al-Sadiq's divorce from Umm Ali regarding the Khawarij?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kadhi* highlights the Imam’s personal engagement with theological diversity within his household, specifically the lingering Khawarij influence on Umm Ali, which necessitated a night of patient persuasion (*i'dar*) before divorce. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ijtihad* and the validity of differing opinions, illustrating that marital dissolution can stem from fundamental doctrinal misalignment rather than mere personal incompatibility. The detail of the Armenian carpet serves as a tangible link to the material culture and trade networks of the era, grounding the spiritual lesson in historical reality.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Ismail Al Maysami, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’farasws and heasws was seated upon a chattel, so I went on to touch the chattel with my hand, so heasws said: ‘This which you are touching with your hand, is Armany (Armenian)’. So I said to himasws, ‘And what have youasws to do with Al-Armany?’. So heasws said: ‘This is a chattel which the mother of Ali came with’, a wife of hisasws’. So when it was another time, I went over to himasws, so I went on to touch what was beneath me, so heasws said: ‘It is as if you want to see what is beneath you’. So I said, ‘No, but the blind tend to tamper’. So heasws said to me: ‘That chattel was for the mother of Ali, and she used to view by the opinions of the Khawarijites, so Iasws respited her for a night up to the morning that she might retract from her opinion, and accept the Wilayah of Amir Al-Momineenasws, but she refrained to measws. So when it was the morning, Iasws divorced her’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people from Ali ibn ’Isma‘il al- Maythamiy from abu al-Jarud who have said the following:

“I once visited abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He was sitting on a certain furnishing. I kept touching it with my hand. He (the Imam) said, ‘What you are touching is from Armenia.’ I then asked, ‘What do you have to do with Armenia?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is what mother of Ali (wife of the Imam) has brought.’ I then visited him at another time and kept touching what I was sitting on. He (the Imam) said, ‘It seems you like to see what is underneath you.’ I replied, ‘No, but a blind only plays.’ He (the Imam) said, to me, ‘That item of belonging was owned by mother of Ali. She was of the opinion of al-Khawarij and I wanted that she can return from her opinion until the morning and accept the divine authority of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, but she refused; then in the morning I divorced her.’”
